newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court said ship legally seized under sanctions law.
newsitem.headline: Court said ship legally seized under sanctions law.

text.p: The European Court of Justice ruled on Thursday that sanctions adopted under Community and Italian law authorized the seizure of a ship and its cargo found in the territoral waters of Yugoslavia in 1994.
The sanctions, lifted last year, are no longer in effect.

In April, 1994, the "Lido II", flying a Maltese flag, and bound for Croatia began to take on water. A helicopter from the NATO/WEU forces landed on its deck and a Dutch military squad took control of the vessel, escorting it to Brindisi, Italy.
Once in Brindisi, the ship and cargo were seized by the Prefect of the Province.

The European Union, implementing sanctions imposed by the United Nations in 1993, adopted a Council regulation prohibiting commercial marine traffic into Yugoslavia. Italy transposed the regulation into national law the following year.

Discounting arguments from the governments of Italy, France and Britain, the court said the regulation applied to ships no matter what flag they operated under, and that confiscations could take place outside the Community.
"The prohibition on entry into the territorial sea of Yugoslavia...can be breached only outside Community territory," the court said.
The court said Community regulations only permit the confiscation of a ship or its cargo once an infringement has been established, and that determination is left to national courts.

The court accepted that "a system of strict criminal liability is not in itself a violation of Community law" and it is for the national court to determine whether a penalty is effective, proportionate and dissuasive.
EXCERPTS FROM THE JUDGMENT
"Sanctions against the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia - Conduct in international waters - Confiscation of a vessel and its cargo"
Reference from the Consiglio di Stato (Italy) for a preliminary ruling in the proceedings pending before that court between
Ebony Maritime SA, Loten Navigation Co. Ltd
and
Prefetto della Provincia di Brindisi and Others

on the interpretation of article 1(1)(c) and (d) and article 10 of Council regulation (EEC) No 990/93 of 26 April 1993 concerning trade between the European Economic Community and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia (Serbia and Montengegro) (OJ 1993 L 102, p. 14) and of article 1(c) and (d) and article 10 of decision 93/235/ECSC of the representatives of governments of the member states meeting within the Council, of 26 April 1993, concerning trade between the European Coal and Steel Community and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia (Serbia and Montenegro)(OJ 1993 L 102, p. 17)
THE COURT hereby rules

1. Article 1(1)(c) and (d) and article 10 of Council regulation (EEC) No 990/93 of 26 April 1993 concerning trade between the European Economic Community and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia (Serbia and Montengegro) prohibits not only the actual entry of commercial traffic into the territorial sea of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia but also conduct occurring in international waters which gives good reason to believe that the vessel concerned is on course for that territorial sea for the purposes of commercial traffic.

2. A domestic provision which, in the event of an ascertained breach of any of the prohibitions laid down in article 1 of the regulation, prescribes confiscation of the cargo carried by one of the means of transport indicated in the second paragraph of article 10 of the regulation is compatible with the regulation, in particular with article 10 thereof.
